ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen all direct and indirect shareholders, directors, officers, authorized signatories, controllers, and identified UBOs before incorporation and periodically thereafter against Canadian sanctions under the United Nations Act, Special Economic Measures Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and Criminal Code terrorist-property provisions; applicable United Nations Security Council lists; OFAC sanctions lists where United States nexus, correspondent banking, U.S. persons, or U.S.-dollar processing is involved; and adverse-media, law-enforcement, insolvency, fraud, corruption, and regulatory databases. Apply enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, heads of international organizations, family members, and close associates under the PCMLTFA framework. Obtain source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence where risk warrants it. A Canadian private company is not required to make its BC transparency register publicly available, but it must maintain it and provide access to specified authorities and law-enforcement bodies.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services, administered by the Province of British Columbia; name requests are submitted through the BC Name Request service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A British Columbia company name must comply with the Business Corporations Act and Business Corporations Regulation. The name must be distinguishable from existing reserved, registered, or otherwise protected names and must not be misleading, obscene, or contrary to public policy. English and French names are generally acceptable. Names may include non-Latin characters only where accepted by the registry and capable of reliable examination and registration; a Roman-character transliteration and an English or French operating name should be prepared for banking, payment processing, tax, and contractual use. The legal name must include an approved corporate designation such as Limited, Ltd., Corporation, Corp., Incorporated, Inc., or another permitted designation. A ULC designation is not itself a standard mandatory legal suffix and should be confirmed with the registry and incorporation professional before filing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying governmental, Indigenous, charitable, financial, insurance, or regulated professional status
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit a name request through BC Name Request with at least three ranked alternatives, a clear business description, and supporting consent or authorization for protected or sensitive terms. A reservation is ordinarily valid for 56 days. If rejected, revise the proposed names and resubmit with the registry's rejection reason addressed; obtain written consent or ministerial, regulator, or institutional approval where required. British Columbia does not provide a general merits-based administrative appeal mechanism for an ordinary name-request rejection. If the decision is alleged to be procedurally unfair, unreasonable, or based on an error of law, seek written reconsideration where available and consider judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, subject to applicable limitation periods. Do not use the rejected name commercially before approval and registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A BC company must maintain a registered office and records office in British Columbia, each with a physical delivery address and mailing address as required by the Business Corporations Act. A commercial virtual-office provider may be used if it supplies a genuine eligible physical address, accepts service of process, maintains required corporate records or makes them available, and satisfies the provider's compliance procedures. A mere mailbox, unverifiable address, or address lacking reliable service-receipt capability is not sufficient. For a digital magazine and sponsored-media business, a virtual office may be legally acceptable at formation, but payment processors, banks, advertisers, tax authorities, and counterparties may require evidence of operational substance, management location, editorial activity, contracts, website control, and beneficial ownership.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official annual probability is published. Routine unannounced corporate-registry inspection is not a standard BC incorporation procedure; practical risk is low for a compliant low-risk digital publisher, but can become material and case-triggered following complaints, suspected misrepresentation, sanctions concerns, tax indicators, service-of-process failure, AML alerts, or inconsistent information supplied to banks and payment processors.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. 57, as amended (BCCA); key statutory provisions: s. 10 (incorporation by filing Notice of Articles), s. 11 (certificate and legal capacity of the company), ss. 51-53 (registered office and records office), and ss. 121-128 (first directors, officers, and share certificates). Federal CBCA does not apply to BC-incorporated ULCs; ULC status is authorized under BCCA Part 1 and the Notice of Articles must designate the company as an unlimited liability company.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (BC Registry Services), Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia; Corporate Online portal (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca); paper filings addressed to Registrar of Companies, PO Box 9431 Stn Prov Govt, Victoria, BC V8W 9V3, Canada.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) filed under s. 10(1) BCCA; the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under s. 11 BCCA; optional supporting instruments include Articles (Form 2), Incorporation Agreement (Form 3), and name approval certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a BC Unlimited Liability Company, and no escrow account or capital deposit is required at incorporation; subscribers may subscribe for shares at nominal consideration. Paid-up capital for tax purposes should be intentionally established at issuance in accordance with subparagraph 89(1)(b)(ii) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) where pass-through treatment is intended.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: The Notice of Articles and Articles filed under the Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, are adopted and ratified as the charter documents of the company. The share subscriptions recorded in the Subscription Journal are approved; shares are allotted and issued to the subscribers against full payment of the subscription price. The registered office shall be the address in the Notice of Articles, and the records office shall be maintained at that location. The following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until successor appointment. Certified by the Corporate Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Approval and Conflicting Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Name Request service (www.bcregistry.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS-funded search on each proposed corporate name. Submit the Name Request application online, listing up to three proposed names in priority order; include the mandatory legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'. Pay the prescribed name request fee (approximately CAD 30). The Registrar provides a Name Approval Certificate with a 56-day reservation; if a numbered company is preferred, incorporation may proceed using the incorporation number and the ULC designation.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report (dated within 90 days)
Signed authorization of incorporator or corporate agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar flags a proposed name as confusingly similar, obtain a written consent letter from the conflicting name holder or resubmit the Name Request with a distinct alternative name; file a reconsideration request with BC Registries, and ultimately pursue judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia if the refusal is maintained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Charter Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia legal counsel or notary public engaged by the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Notice of Articles (Form 1) setting out the ULC company class, authorized share structure (including class rights and par value or no-par designation), first directors, municipal address of the registered office in BC, and the records office address. Adopt Articles (Form 2), either the BCCA Model Articles or bespoke articles, and prepare the Incorporation Agreement (Form 3). Each incorporator and each named first director must execute the documents and sign Consent to Act as Director. Verify that all addresses are a physical street address in British Columbia and not a post office box.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles (Form 2) or adoption of Model Articles
Consent to Act as Director for each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend and re-execute any defective schedule before submission; if a defect is identified post-filing, submit a corrective Notice of Articles amendment and pay the prescribed correction fee, or apply to the Registrar for voluntary correction under BCCA within the statutory correction window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance — Corporate Online portal (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to Corporate Online, select 'File an Incorporation Application,' and upload the executed Notice of Articles, Articles, incorporation agreement, name approval (if any), and director consents. Pay the online incorporation filing fee (CAD 375; paper filing CAD 450). The date of filing becomes the incorporation date, and the system-generated Certificate of Incorporation is conclusive evidence that the company exists and has the capacity of a natural person under s. 11 BCCA.
required_dossiers: Consents to Act as Director for all first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition for correction, file a revised Notice of Articles through Corporate Online before the requisition deadline; if incorporation is refused, apply for judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia and correct the identified deficiencies in a fresh filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office, Records Office, and Corporate Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary or registered agent in British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the registered office and records office are located at the physical BC street address stated in the Notice of Articles. Assemble the corporate records binder containing the Certificate of Incorporation, Notice of Articles, Articles, register of directors, register of shareholders, share transfer register, and minutes of director and shareholder meetings. The registers and records must be available for statutory inspection at the records office during normal business hours, except where the BCCA permits records to be held elsewhere.
required_dossiers: Register of Shareholders and share transfer ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office or records office address is invalid or relocated, file the applicable change form with the BC Registrar (Form 10 for registered office and Form 11 for records office) within the prescribed period and update the registers accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Organizational Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; presided by the Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the Board to ratify the Notice of Articles and Articles, adopt the First Board Resolution approving share subscriptions, appoint the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, authorize the opening of corporate bank accounts, and establish signing authorities. Where physical assembly is impractical, pass resolutions by written consent of all directors in accordance with BCCA procedure. Record all decisions in the minutes and file the executed First Board Resolution in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Notice of First Board Meeting or written consent resolution
Minutes of First Board Meeting (including First Board Resolution)
Share subscription journal and allotment schedule
Bank account opening resolutions and authorized signatory list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the meeting is challenged for procedural defect or a banker or counterparty questions authority, pass a curative director resolution, produce certified minutes, and re-execute officer appointment documents to confirm incumbent authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number Registration and Mandatory Program Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online (www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-individuals/online-registration.html)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly incorporated ULC with the Canada Revenue Agency using the Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN). Activate the GST/HST program account where annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000, and register for the BC provincial sales tax (PST) account if taxable goods or services are supplied in British Columbia. The BN is the master identifier used by BC Registries, financial institutions, and federal and provincial regulators for the entity's ongoing compliance lifecycle.
required_dossiers: List of first directors and officers with personal identification
Registered office and records office address confirmation
Bank account details for CRA refund routing (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA application is queried due to registry record mismatch, reconcile the corporate registry data through BC Registries first, then resubmit the BN application; if a BN is issued erroneously, request correction via the CRA Business Account portal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — digital magazine publishing is a knowledge-based commercial activity with no physical manufacturing in British Columbia; no industrial licensing board authorization is required under provincial law. The only administrative body of relevance is the municipal or district licensing office in the municipality where the registered office is located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (general office/digital media classification) issued by the local municipality, e.g., City of Vancouver Business Licence for 'Digital Media — Office Operation'; no provincial industrial operating permit or sectoral manufacturing licence applies to a digital magazine portal.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (federal) and British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (provincial)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — a pure digital publishing and sponsored media portal does not trigger review under the federal Impact Assessment Act or the BC Environmental Assessment Act; no full EIA Report or registration certificate is required for a leased office premises with no physical industrial facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial discharge or volatile organic compound (VOC) emission limits are triggered by a digital office operation; office sanitary effluent is limited to municipal sewer discharge under the BC Municipal Wastewater Regulation (applicable daily maxima where an on-site sewage works exists: BOD 300 mg/L and TSS 350 mg/L, not anticipated). Any ancillary warehousing of printed magazines would invoke the BC Recycling Regulation stewardship obligations for printed paper and packaging, and the Spill Reporting Regulation threshold for reportable discharges.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety compliance under the BC Fire Code and National Fire Code of Canada 2020, including annual fire safety inspection of the leased office premises and a documented fire safety plan; structural load certification for the occupied floor area under the BC Building Code; and occupational health and safety clearance through WorkSafeBC registration under the Workers Compensation Act, with compliance to the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation (ergonomics, electrical safety, and emergency preparedness). No specialized civil defense permit is required for a non-hazardous digital media office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Federal tax authority for goods and services tax/harmonized sales tax and income tax; BC Ministry of Finance for provincial sales tax. Primary portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/register-your-business.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The BC ULC, as a Canadian resident corporation, obtains a federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account via CRA's online registration service or Form RC1. Process: (1) Incorporate under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act; (2) Register the corporation for a BN through CRA's 'Start a Business' online service or RC1; (3) Open a GST/HST account simultaneously; (4) Register with the BC Ministry of Finance for PST if the entity makes taxable supplies within BC; (5) Maintain corporate records, director residency information, and place-of-management details for ongoing tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No direct check-the-box equivalent under Canadian federal income tax; however, the BC ULC is eligible for the Canada-US Tax Treaty Article IV(7) election to be treated as a resident of either Canada or the US for treaty purposes. Additionally, a US check-the-box election may be made on Form 8832 to classify the ULC as a corporation or disregarded entity for US federal tax purposes. Canadian hybrid mismatch rules under Income Tax Act Part VI.1 and s.163.3 allow certain elective alignment provisions for cross-border arrangements involving hybrid entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) combined with BC PST (Provincial Sales Tax) as a separate levy; not harmonized
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies for mandatory GST/HST registration; non-residents providing digital supplies to Canadian consumers may require simplified registration; BC PST registration required when making taxable sales of goods or specifically listed services in British Columbia
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, or digital stamping regime in Canada. CRA accepts electronic invoices; GST/HST returns must be filed electronically for monthly filers and large businesses. Digital records must be retained in an accessible and readable format when kept electronically.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of digital magazine portal subscriptions and sponsored media placements to non-residents are zero-rated under the Excise Tax Act where the recipient is a non-resident, the supply is for consumption outside Canada, and applicable place-of-supply rules are satisfied. Specifically, Schedule VI, Part V (services) and Part VII (intangible personal property) zero-rating provisions apply when the recipient is not resident in Canada and the value of the supply is not attributable to use in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial contracts or terms-of-service evidencing the non-resident recipient and place of supply
Subscriber records and digital access logs confirming location of the recipient
Invoices and bank/Payment Gateway settlement records proving the consideration received and repatriation of funds
Foreign tax identification number or residency certificate of the non-resident customer
CRA Form GST190 or similar supporting export documentation where physical media is distributed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess a claim of zero-rating within four years of the assessment, or indefinitely in cases of misrepresentation or fraud. Erroneous zero-rating triggers immediate GST/HST assessment, interest on the arrears, and penalties including gross negligence penalties of up to 50% of the net tax, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion. The CRA strictly reviews place-of-supply indicators and non-resident status evidence, and failure to substantiate export supplies can result in retrospective clawback of input tax credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC), operating in conjunction with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for bank supervision and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for anti-money laundering compliance; foreign exchange administration is liberalized with no separate central bank FX approval regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Canada maintains no exchange control restrictions on the inflow or outflow of funds for trade, dividends, interest, or repatriation of capital. Profit remittances by a BC Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) are permitted without prior regulatory consent, subject only to corporate law solvency tests and applicable tax compliance under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the BC Income Tax Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts in Canada. Export proceeds may be retained in Canadian dollars or foreign currency at the entity's discretion; no surrender requirement to the central bank or government authority exists. Only general anti-money laundering recordkeeping and reporting obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) apply to cross-border transfers exceeding CAD 10,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility with strict legal constraints. Foreign digital EMI-type payment institutions are not recognized as banks in Canada; to offer payment services, an entity must be registered as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and may require provincial licensing in British Columbia under the Money Services Act. Offshore EMIs that are not so registered cannot maintain direct clearing access to Canadian payment rails; they may be used only as a supplementary collection channel with clear contractual segregation of client funds and full compliance with Canadian data residency and PIPEDA obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most Canadian tier-1 banks permit fully remote account opening for non-face-to-face corporate clients, subject to enhanced due diligence. Physical presence of directors is not an absolute mandate, but banks may request an in-person interview for high-risk jurisdictions or complex ownership structures. For a ULC with non-resident ownership, a video-conference KYC interview, certified true copies of corporate registers, and notarized identification are generally acceptable, supplemented by a BC registered office and a Canadian resident compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner concentration (single or majority ownership via ULC pass-through)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate org chart with all ultimate beneficial owners, government-issued photo IDs and passports, proof of source of wealth (audited financial statements, tax returns, or sale documents), bank references from incumbent financial institutions, and a written explanation of the ULC pass-through structure with supporting legal opinion from Canadian counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure in payment flows (AdSense / Stripe receipts from diverse geographies)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geographic revenue breakdown by payment processor, transactional history demonstrating low average ticket size and digital content delivery, commercial contracts with advertisers and subscribers, and a documented AML compliance policy covering sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, and geographic risk scoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns for a digital media entity (large lump-sum sponsor payments versus organically recurring revenue)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sponsorship/insertion orders, invoicing and settlement schedules, proof of content delivery or ad impressions, bank statements showing intra-group flow trail, and board-approved revenue recognition policy under IFRS 15.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions to the ULC are routed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the non-resident parent or shareholder using a permitted Canadian bank and purpose code e.g., 'Capital contribution to Canadian entity' (enterprise code 512/513 under Statistics Canada reporting, if applicable). The Canadian receiving bank will require supporting documentation: signed shareholder resolution, subscription agreement, AML source-of-funds evidence, and confirmation that the ULC has no minimum paid-up capital requirement under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act. Amounts above CAD 100,000 may trigger FINTRAC reporting, and any inward transfer exceeding CAD 10 million is subject to the Currency Transactions Report (CTR) and Foreign Money Laundering Reporting requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for digital magazine services are cleared via standard SWIFT MT103 payment orders for invoices and royalty payments, and commercial letters of credit (LC) are available but normally unnecessary for intangible digital services. Recurring disbursements to foreign technology platforms (e.g., server providers, contractors) may be batched through the bank's host-to-host channel or API-based cash management dashboard. All outward wire transfers require the bank's standard AML/fraud screening, and non-resident supplier invoices should be supported by a valid contract, beneficiary bank details, and applicable withholding tax certificates (e.g., Part XIII or Part XIV of the Income Tax Act).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX swaps (CAD/USD and other G10 crosses)
Outright FX forwards with tenors up to 12 months, subject to ISDA or bank master agreement
FX options (European style) for hedging translational and transactional exposure
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for medium-term non-resident loan repayment streams
NDFs are permitted in theory but rarely necessary because the Canadian dollar is fully convertible and deliverable onshore; they are used only for illiquid exotic currency pairs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after each anniversary of incorporation or continuation; e.g., a June 30 anniversary creates a filing deadline of August 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 200; failure to file annual reports for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off from the BC corporate register, with dissolution and possible restoration under the BC Business Corporations Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the return is due June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; CRA may also issue arbitrary assessments and charge interest on unpaid balances

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST annual return (only if GST/HST registered or annual reporting period assigned)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual filers; quarterly and monthly filers must follow the periods set by CRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file on time triggers a penalty of 5% of the amount due plus 1% per month up to 12 months, together with interest and possible CRA redesignation of the filing frequency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and minute book review (internal corporate record reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records maintained at the registered office; available for inspection by the BC Registrar, CRA, authorities, and shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, alongside preparation of the BC Annual Report and before finalizing the year's general meeting resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct filing penalty; defective registers can invalidate corporate actions, expose directors to liability, and may result in a Registrar compliance order requiring record production

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No asset, revenue, or employee threshold in BC compels a private ULC to have a statutory audit. An external audit is mandatory only if the ULC is a reporting issuer or public company, or if shareholders validly require the appointment of an auditor; otherwise, shareholders may waive or dispense with the auditor appointment under the BC Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP for private enterprises (CPA Canada Handbook Part II – ASPE) is available for a private BC ULC; IFRS is mandatory if the entity becomes a reporting issuer or publicly accountable enterprise. CRA tax accounting is based on the chosen GAAP framework subject to Income Tax Act adjustments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BC does not require an annual UBO filing with the Registrar. The BC ULC must maintain a transparency register and annually take reasonable steps to identify significant individuals. Transfers or acquisitions of shares that make an individual a significant individual, or cease such status, must be recorded in the transparency register within 15 days of the company becoming aware. The register must be available to CRA, the RCMP, and other prescribed authorities, and must be reviewed at least annually in conjunction with the corporate annual return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $150 - $500 per year for a BC registered and records office service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000 - $12,000 per year if a voluntary audit is obtained; no audit fee is required for a private ULC that has validly waived the auditor appointment

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (Federal Part I general rate 15% + British Columbia provincial general rate 12%; no small business deduction because the ULC is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation when owned by a US shareholder)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-CCPC status eliminates the 9% federal / 2% BC small-business rates. Potential credits: (i) SR&ED investment tax credit (15% non-refundable federal) for eligible software development; (ii) BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (17.5%, enhanced 25% for STEAM content) if the magazine portal qualifies as an interactive digital media product; (iii) BC Film/Book Publishing Tax Credits are not applicable to periodical publishers. No statutory tax holiday applies.
